correctness.rationale: The FD and ID jointly make any consistent subrelation a partial permutation; a feasible strict extension is precisely a nonempty cross-part permutation on unused vertices; a pair of unused vertices in different parts gives a two-cycle. A cyclic rotation by m=max s_i explicitly proves allowed-permutation existence iff 2m≤s. Disjoint forbidden within-part rook placements yield the exact inclusion-exclusion polynomial, and largest-part omissions give every size in [max(n-a1,2a2), min(n,2(n-a1))]. Other omission parts cannot escape this interval. Independent exhaustive enumerations and the packaged checker corroborate small cases; finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Source/claim/alias/parameter searches did not locate the full claimed theorem. Direct inspection of the closest published complete-multipartite paired-domination result shows even-cardinality support feasibility but not oriented permutation counts, FD+ID repairs, or odd-length maximal cycle covers. The 2026 and 2024 database/argumentation papers set the context but prove general correspondence and complexity, not this multipartite size polynomial or no-gap interval. The 2020 repair-counting result is for prioritized FD settings, not simultaneous FD and ID on the explicit multipartite instance. Hall-type feasibility and rook polynomial inclusion-exclusion are acknowledged standard; genuine residual risk is equivalent older maximal partial derangement enumeration.
residual_risks: Older combinatorial literature could contain the same enumerator formulated as maximal partial permutations or maximal directed cycle packings avoiding block-diagonal arrows; synonym searches were not exhaustive.
The 2020 counting paper was inspected in accessible HTML text, not its complete PDF, leaving some residual risk of hidden stronger specialization.
The general setting is historically known; only the specific exact polynomial, maximality classification and no-gap spectrum are claimed as new, never basic Hall/rook methods.

value.rationale: A complete finite-team and integrity-constraint repair classification for an infinite, naturally structured family, including exact labelled repair-size polynomial and a sharp gap-free size spectrum. It provides a nontrivial tractable instance in the setting of coupled FD and ID repairs (general cases have hardness results), a benchmark for repairs and argumentation encodings, and exposes odd cycle contributions omitted by matching-only counts. The combinatorial classification and qualitative interval are more than routine recomputation or a single arbitrary finite invariant.
